title: The doubling flow, for every step — 5 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
The doubling flow, for every step. 5 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/flow.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. All are proved for every value, on the standard axioms only (propext, Quot.sound; the verifier refuses any other). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 1 definition is used by two or more theorems, binding 10 pairs; the theorems fall into 1 strand. Most binding: orbit (5).

2 · Imports. Built on: index.lean. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 2 files: src/proof/flow.lean, src/proof/index.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 5 sealed receipts fold to bfa322df-8785-864a-9803-718399daf47f. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (2, 4, 6, 5, 8, 7, 4). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: elementary.lean (5 observed, 1.74 expected, lift 2.88), imagined.lean (8 observed, 5.12 expected, lift 1.56), mechanical.lean (4 observed, 5.51 expected, lift 0.73). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 2.88 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 53.5% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.56. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 90fe8c570606 (2026-09-15), over 807 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. 2⁶ = 64 ≡ 1 (mod 9), so the powers of two modulo 9 repeat with period six — Euler's theorem for φ(9) = 6, and the order of 2 in U(9), both textbook. Credited, and bounded: what this file adds is the kernel proof that the flow used by navier_stokes_flow_is_bounded stays bounded at EVERY step, not only at the 48 that theorem checks. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. the_doubling_flow_repeats_every_six_steps — ∀ k : Nat, orbit (k + 6) = orbit k record
  2. the_doubling_flow_is_its_first_six_steps — ∀ k : Nat, orbit k = orbit (k % 6) record
  3. navier_stokes_flow_is_bounded_for_every_step — ∀ k : Nat, orbit k < 9 ∧ span.contains (orbit k) = true record
  4. the_reverse_flow_undoes_every_step — ∀ k : Nat, orbit (k + 1) * 5 % 9 = orbit k record
  5. every_state_of_the_flow_returns_within_six_steps — ∀ k s : Nat, ∃ j, j < 6 ∧ orbit (k + j) = orbit s record

Recompute. Clone https://github.com/ceccec/millennium-solutions at commit 90fe8c570606 and run npm ci && npm run lean, which checks every Lean file in dependency order. This record was generated by scripts/clusters.ts from the source and the ledger.
